docs.D00_original_thesis.md:
Title: Original investment rationale and the limits of the recovered record
Source: compiled from: https://www.reuters.com/article/markets/stocks/ackmans-pershing-square-takes-big-stakes-in-freddie-fannie-idUSBRE9AE0TO; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2014/09/08113002/PSH-Annual-Report.pdf
Date: 2015-03-24

Pershing publicly disclosed the common-stock investment in November 2013. Reuters reported an approximately $500 million commitment and ownership of 9.98% of outstanding Fannie common and 9.77% of Freddie common. These are existing-share percentages, not ownership after Treasury exercises its warrants. The exact first execution date and a verified original 2013 purchase letter are not recovered.

The nearest authenticated detailed letter used here is the March 24, 2015 annual report, which describes the investment and its reasoning retrospectively. It is public well before this pack's January 2025 cutoff, but must not be mislabeled a contemporaneous 2013 quotation.

The letter says: “we believe that there is no credible alternative to replace them.” It connects the companies' role to the availability of the 30-year, prepayable, fixed-rate mortgage and argues that a renewed, recapitalized system is preferable to shutting them down.

It also states: “We view this net worth sweep as an unlawful taking of shareholders’ private property”. This is Pershing's legal position, not an adjudicated conclusion that Treasury's claim is invalid. Enterprise profitability and shareholder rights are different parts of the thesis.

The underlying economic proposition is that essential guarantee franchises can generate substantial recurring earnings if allowed to retain capital and operate under a viable regulatory arrangement. The security proposition is more contingent: common owners need a resolution of senior claims and government control that leaves meaningful value after dilution.

The letter records buying additional shares after the September 2014 adverse district-court ruling and concentrating legal resources on constitutional takings claims. Thus the investor's willingness to hold through adverse developments is documented; it does not establish that every legal theory succeeded.

For the current reassessment, the original thesis supplies four tests: the franchises remain necessary; underlying earnings can rebuild capital; government policy can evolve toward recapitalization; and common shareholders retain sufficient economic participation. A rising share price alone does not satisfy those tests. Nor should a decade of waiting automatically disprove franchise value if the capital structure and policy path are materially different today.
docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Mortgage guarantees, not ordinary unencumbered common equity
Source: compiled from: https://www.fanniemae.com/media/document/pdf/q32024release.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1026214/000102621424000098/a20243qerexhibit991.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052224000632/fnm-20240930.htm
Date: 2024-10-31

Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are separate government-sponsored mortgage-finance enterprises. They buy eligible mortgages, support securitization and guarantee mortgage-backed securities. Their function enables lenders to originate and distribute mortgage credit while investors receive securities with defined payment guarantees. Both have single-family and multifamily businesses.

Guarantee fees compensate for credit risk, capital, administration and the support arrangements surrounding the system. Scale, standardization, underwriting data, lender relationships and the depth of mortgage-security markets create valuable franchises. Those advantages coexist with statutory missions and political constraints; the companies are not free to maximize returns without regard to housing policy.

They remain in FHFA conservatorship, begun in 2008. The conservator exercises powers that ordinary shareholders and boards would normally hold. Treasury's senior preferred stock purchase agreements provide financial backing while also placing senior economic claims ahead of common equity.

Treasury holds warrants for 79.9% of each company's common stock on a fully diluted basis after exercise, under their terms. Existing common ownership percentages therefore overstate participation in any normalized earnings pool unless warrant dilution is incorporated. Junior preferred securities have different priority and capped contractual claims.

As of September 30, Fannie reported $90.530 billion net worth and Freddie $56.390 billion. These accounting capital balances are not freely distributable common equity. Treasury liquidation preferences, regulatory capital requirements and contractual restrictions must be analyzed separately.

Fannie CEO Priscilla Almodovar emphasizes supporting housing and increasing net worth. Management operates under government oversight; a good quarterly result cannot unilaterally end conservatorship, cancel Treasury claims or authorize common dividends.

A conventional company analysis asks whether earnings are durable and reinvestment attractive. Here the analyst must add a second question: who owns the economic benefit under current and potential future contracts? The businesses can earn billions while reported common EPS is near zero or negative because amounts accrue to senior preferred interests. Market capitalization divided by total enterprise net income is consequently not a valid ordinary common P/E.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Earnings rebuild net worth, but not unrestricted common capital
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052224000185/fnma2023q4pressrelease.htm; https://www.fanniemae.com/media/document/pdf/q32024_financial_supplement.pdf; https://www.freddiemac.com/investors/financials/pdf/2023er-4q23_release.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1026214/000102621424000098/a20243qerexhibit991.htm
Date: 2024-10-31

Both companies use December fiscal years. Full-year 2024 results have not been released. Financial-company net revenues and net worth are more relevant here than industrial EBITDA, capex or conventional net debt.

| Metric, $bn | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | Q3 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fannie net income | 22.176 | 12.923 | 17.408 | 4.044 |
| Fannie year/quarter-end net worth | 47.4 | 60.3 | 77.7 | 90.530 |
| Freddie net income | Not recovered | 9.327 | 10.538 | 3.105 |

Fannie 2023 net revenues were $29.048 billion versus $29.735 billion in 2022, down 2%. Freddie Q3 2024 net revenues were $5.838 billion, up approximately 3% year over year, with net worth of $56.390 billion. A fully matched three-year revenue and expense table for both companies is not recovered.

Fannie's Q3 income declined from $4.484 billion in Q2, partly because fair-value gains and the benefit for credit losses declined. Nine-month income was $12.848 billion. Net worth increased by approximately $4.047 billion during Q3.

Freddie's Q3 net income increased $420 million year over year. The comparison benefits from an additional $313 million expense accrual in the prior-year quarter. Its earnings improvement is therefore not all recurring revenue growth.

GAAP common EPS does not equal total net income divided by existing legal common shares because senior preferred allocations and warrant-related share treatment matter. Freddie's release shows approximately 3.234 billion weighted-average common shares for EPS calculations; that is not a claim that every Treasury warrant has already been exercised.

There are no ordinary common dividends or buybacks to capitalize as current shareholder distributions. Capital retention builds accounting net worth while liquidation preferences can also increase. A conventional FCF yield, EV/EBITDA or net-debt ratio is not meaningful without a financial-institution balance-sheet framework.

The key financial sensitivity is normalized after-credit-loss earnings relative to required regulatory capital, followed by the allocation of that capital and earnings among Treasury, junior preferred and common holders.
docs.D03_latest_results.md:
Title: Latest operating results before the policy decision window
Source: compiled from: https://www.fanniemae.com/media/document/pdf/q32024release.pdf; https://www.fanniemae.com/media/document/pdf/q32024_financial_supplement.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1026214/000102621424000098/a20243qerexhibit991.htm
Date: 2024-10-31

Fannie reported Q3 results October 31, with $4.044 billion net income and $90.530 billion net worth. The release says it supported $274 billion of housing activity through the first nine months of 2024. These figures illustrate continuing operating scale while conservatorship remains in place.

CEO Priscilla Almodovar said: “Our net worth increased to $90.5 billion and, since the start of the year, we’ve reduced our minimum regulatory capital shortfall by $17 billion.” A declining shortfall is progress, not a statement that every regulatory buffer has been satisfied.

Compared with Q2, Fannie's net income declined $440 million. Fair-value gains fell to $52 million from $447 million, while net interest income was relatively stable. Credit-loss provisioning and fair values can make quarterly earnings variable even when the guarantee book remains large.

Freddie reported October 30. Q3 net income was $3.105 billion and net revenues $5.838 billion. Net worth rose to $56.390 billion, compared with approximately $44.7 billion a year earlier. The company said it helped 415,000 households during the quarter.

Freddie's income increase of $420 million year over year partly reflects lower noninterest expense because the prior period included a $313 million additional accrual. An analyst should not annualize the entire year-over-year increase as a permanent growth rate.

Freddie's senior preferred liquidation preference was $125.871 billion at September 30 and was scheduled to increase with retained net worth under the governing terms. Net worth accumulation is therefore not equivalent to erasing the senior claim. The same conceptual distinction applies to Fannie.

Neither earnings release supplies an approved plan for IPO, relisting or release from conservatorship. Neither company forecasts a distributable common dividend or confirms that Treasury will deem its senior preferred repaid. Those matters depend on contracts, regulation and government decisions beyond the operating teams' quarterly execution.

As of January 15, these are still the latest published earnings. No Q4 2024 results, January 16 investor deck or subsequent government action is imported into the financial baseline. A favorable policy scenario must be labeled as a scenario layered on top of the observed earnings.
docs.D04_price_valuation.md:
Title: The election rally and the difference between market price and scenario value
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/FNMA?period1=1727740800&period2=1736985600&interval=1d; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/FMCC?period1=1727740800&period2=1736985600&interval=1d; https://x.com/BillAckman/status/1873818034428694837; https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/bill-ackman-expects-trump-privatize-fannie-mae-freddie-mac-2024-12-30
Date: 2025-01-15

The date-bounded historical series gives January 15 closes of $6.21 for FNMA and $5.66 for FMCC. Volumes were 46,566,200 and 19,818,800 shares, respectively. The instruments are OTC common stocks, with trading and ownership considerations different from a major-exchange constituent.

For context, October 1 closes were $1.17 and $1.14. Those starting observations precede the November election. By January 15 the calculated increases were approximately 431% and 396%, respectively. The observation window's intraday highs were $7.80 FNMA and $7.15 FMCC, putting the closes approximately 20.4% and 20.8% below those highs. These are October-to-January observations, not a verified 52-week range.

Average daily volume during that window was approximately 16.46 million FNMA and 7.47 million FMCC. Liquidity rose around policy events, but a highly liquid rally can still reverse when expectations change.

Reuters's December 30 report says the shares gained 18.4% and 18% after Ackman's post. His post estimates approximately $34 intrinsic value per share at hypothetical 2026 IPOs and assumes approximately $31 offering prices. These are investor scenarios, not consensus targets or government-approved transaction prices.

At $6.21 and $5.66, the gap to $34 is large, but depends on senior-preferred treatment, warrant exercise, regulatory capital and any new issuance. A probability-weighted valuation must include unfavorable outcomes, including heavy dilution or indefinite conservatorship. It is not enough to divide the target by the current price.

An ordinary trailing common P/E is not meaningful because total enterprise net income is not currently available to common shareholders. EV/EBITDA is similarly unsuitable for these mortgage-finance balance sheets. Point-in-time fully diluted market capitalization, consensus common EPS and a long-run normalized multiple history are not recovered.

The existing holder faces a different question from a new buyer: whether the rally sufficiently discounts a more credible policy path, or whether the remaining conditional upside still outweighs the unchanged contractual risks.

The answer requires explicit probabilities and security-level dilution assumptions.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Political enthusiasm does not settle seniority, dilution or mortgage costs
Source: compiled from: https://www.cnn.com/2024/12/02/economy/fannie-mae-freddie-mac-mortgage-rates-housing/index.html; https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2767; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052225000004/fnm-20250102.htm; https://x.com/BillAckman/status/1873818034428694837
Date: 2025-01-15

CNN's December 2 report says privatization is widely expected under the incoming Trump administration, but warns that changing the government relationship could unsettle mortgage investors and increase borrowing costs. That is a policy tradeoff: maximizing the share value of the enterprises is not necessarily the government's sole objective.

No new, directly authenticated pre-January15 Trump promise specifying cancellation of senior preferred, warrant terms or a relisting date is recovered here. Expectations based on the first administration's unfinished reform effort must not be represented as an enacted second-term plan.

The January 2 Treasury/FHFA amendments restore Treasury's consent right over release from conservatorship. The official release states that FHFA will seek public input about the potential effects on housing and financial markets. These requirements can make a release more orderly, but also add process, negotiation and timing uncertainty.

Common holders face several adverse scenarios. Treasury might insist on preserving or converting its senior preferred claim, causing large dilution. A high regulatory capital requirement might require substantial outside equity. A continuing guarantee could require fees that reduce earnings. Political disagreement over housing affordability could delay reform even while the companies remain profitable.

The retained-earnings story also needs care. Accounting net worth is increasing, but current contracts can increase Treasury's liquidation preference alongside retained earnings. A growing balance sheet is therefore not by itself proof of increasing distributable common value.

Ackman himself acknowledged uncertainty in his December 30 post: “There remains a high degree of uncertainty about the ultimate outcome so you should limit your exposure to what you can afford to lose if you choose to invest.” That warning is part of the public thesis, not a disclaimer to be discarded because his upside estimate is attractive.

The constructive case is that profitable franchises and Treasury's potential warrant proceeds align shareholder and taxpayer incentives for a negotiated solution. The bear case is that the sovereign controls the terms and can choose a path with limited value for existing common. Both remain live at the cutoff; the rally does not resolve them.
docs.D06_peer_capital_benchmarks.md:
Title: Capital rules and the limits of the mortgage-insurer comparison
Source: compiled from: https://www.fhfa.gov/document/Fact-Sheet-Final-Rule-Amend-Enterprise-Regulatory-Capital-Framework; https://x.com/BillAckman/status/1873818034428694837; https://www.fanniemae.com/media/document/pdf/q32024release.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1026214/000102621424000098/a20243qerexhibit991.htm
Date: 2024-12-30

Fannie and Freddie are each other's closest franchise comparables. Private mortgage insurers, banks and other guarantors can help test credit economics, but no listed company has an identical combination of government mission, mortgage-security scale, Treasury support and conservatorship restrictions.

The FHFA's February 2022 capital-rule fact sheet states a minimum tier-one leverage ratio of 2.5% of adjusted total assets, plus a leverage buffer. It replaces the earlier fixed 1.5% buffer with a dynamic buffer equal to half the stability capital buffer. Risk-based requirements also apply. Thus “the capital rule is 2.5%” is an incomplete description of the binding framework.

Ackman's December 30 proposal calls for 2.5% of guarantees outstanding. That is his preferred scenario, with a different simplified framing, not evidence that the current buffers and risk-based tests disappear. He argues that such capital could cover nearly seven times actual realized financial-crisis losses.

He compares this with private mortgage insurers that insure a first-loss portion of the mortgage, while GSE guarantees generally cover loans with borrower equity and, where required, mortgage insurance. This is his explanation for why the GSEs can support a lower capital ratio. The comparison should be stress-tested for correlated housing losses, model risk, operating needs and support fees.

At September 30, reported net worth was approximately $90.5 billion Fannie and $56.4 billion Freddie. These are accounting balances. Ackman's December post cites $168 billion combined capital accumulated since the sweep ended in 2019; his “capital” measure should not be silently equated with the two quarter-end GAAP net-worth figures.

A verified table of MGIC/Radian/Essent forward multiples, margins and matching regulatory ratios is not recovered. No present-day peer valuation data are substituted. Capital adequacy is more important here than a superficial cheap P/E comparison.

The analyst must distinguish three questions: whether the guarantee franchises are economically sound; whether a proposed capital requirement is prudent and politically acceptable; and what equity ownership remains after recapitalization. Favorable answers to the first do not automatically establish the second or third.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: From election catalyst to a new consent requirement
Source: compiled from: https://www.cnn.com/2024/12/02/economy/fannie-mae-freddie-mac-mortgage-rates-housing/index.html; https://x.com/BillAckman/status/1873818034428694837; https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2767; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052225000004/fnm-20250102.htm
Date: 2025-01-15

October 30–31, 2024: Freddie and Fannie released profitable Q3 results, with $56.4 billion and $90.5 billion net worth. The operating baseline entering the election was continued retained earnings, not financial distress comparable to 2008.

November 2024: Trump's election generated expectations that the incoming administration could resume the first term's unfinished recapitalization and release effort. This is a political catalyst, not an automatic contractual change. The companies remain in conservatorship.

December 2, 2024: CNN described the anticipated privatization effort and the potential for higher mortgage costs if investors lose confidence in the government relationship. A viable plan needs to address housing-market stability as well as taxpayer and shareholder economics.

December 30, 2024: Ackman publicly outlined a scenario crediting past Treasury payments toward repayment of senior preferred, setting a 2.5% capital requirement and pursuing hypothetical Q4 2026 IPOs. He estimated approximately $34 intrinsic value and $31 offering prices, assuming full Treasury warrant exercise and future government stock sales.

The post explicitly says these holdings have not been good investments to date and acknowledges substantial uncertainty. It announces an intention to share a detailed presentation in the new year, not an already public set of later slides.

January 2, 2025: Treasury and FHFA announced preferred-stock purchase agreement amendments restoring Treasury consent to release. FHFA agreed to a public-input process about market and housing impacts.

January 7, 2025: Fannie's SEC filing described those amendments. Neither the filing nor the official release cancels Treasury's senior preferred, exercises the warrants or lists common stock on an exchange.

January 15, 2025: historical closes are $6.21 FNMA and $5.66 FMCC following a large rally from early October. The outgoing administration remains in office; the incoming administration's detailed implementation choices are unresolved.

The timeline stops on January 15. A later presentation or statement cannot be used to add extra policy details. Current analysis should treat the December30 proposal as advocacy and a scenario, not a completed deal or an authenticated government commitment.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Existing exposure, opportunity cost and the public December thesis
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/07152731/Performance-Report-September-2024-PSH.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2024/03/22201541/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2023-Annual-Report.pdf; https://x.com/BillAckman/status/1873818034428694837
Date: 2024-12-30

The most recent independently recovered firm AUM figure is $18.4988 billion at September 30, including PSVII and bond proceeds. PSH AUM was $15.1353 billion. Neither is a January15 cash balance or the NAV denominator for an exact current position weight.

The public portfolio includes Alphabet, Universal Music, Hilton, Chipotle, Restaurant Brands, Canadian Pacific Kansas City, Howard Hughes, Brookfield and Nike, alongside Fannie/Freddie. Ordinary 13F tables omit OTC positions and foreign-listed holdings, so those tables cannot establish current GSE exposure or complete portfolio weights.

For a dated scale reference, the March2024 annual report's December2023 PSH NAV weights were Universal Music 24.88% directly plus affiliate exposure, Alphabet 14.06%, Chipotle 13.71%, Restaurant Brands approximately13.50%, Hilton12.15%, Howard Hughes11.72% and Canadian Pacific8.70%. These stale fund weights are not January2025 allocations. Current cash and exact GSE economic weight are unavailable.

The same annual report identifies Alphabet as the2023 addition and Lowe's as the exit. Its strategy emphasizes high-quality businesses, capable managers and long-term concentrated ownership. The GSE position differs because realization depends on government policy rather than ordinary corporate execution.

On December30 Ackman wrote: “We have owned Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac common stock for more than a decade. Today, they trade at or around our average cost. As such, they have not been great investments to date.”

He also wrote that there was a credible path to removal from conservatorship “in the next two years.” The statement reflects renewed conviction in a possible policy route, not evidence of a new purchase or a guaranteed deadline.

The manager's choice is therefore an existing-position reassessment after a significant rally. Opportunity cost and sizing matter even if the long-run thesis remains attractive. Exact incremental transactions are not publicly established by the sources here; no ADD execution is inferred from favorable rhetoric.

The public warning to limit exposure to what an investor can lose should remain part of the decision framework. High conviction in a conditional asymmetric payoff is not the same as low downside risk.
docs.D09_what_changed_and_scenario.md:
Title: What changed since purchase, and what must still happen
Source: compiled from: https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sm786; https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/20pdf/19-422_new_l5gm.pdf; https://x.com/BillAckman/status/1873818034428694837; https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2767
Date: 2025-01-15

The original position combined valuable operating franchises with a legal and policy overhang. Several things have changed since2013, but none converts current common into an unencumbered claim on all earnings.

In September2019 Treasury and FHFA allowed greater retention of earnings. Subsequent arrangements continued capital accumulation. The beneficial change is growing accounting resources inside the businesses rather than a perpetual cash sweep. The limiting fact is that Treasury's liquidation preference is not automatically extinguished by retaining earnings.

The Supreme Court's June23,2021 Collins decision rejected the broad statutory challenge to FHFA's authority to enter the relevant amendment and held the director-removal restriction unconstitutional. It did not order wholesale cancellation of the sweep, privatization or a windfall for every common shareholder. The current thesis cannot rest on pretending the litigation has already produced that result.

The2024 election changes the potential administrative decision-makers. Ackman's December30 post therefore shifts attention toward negotiation and recapitalization. He proposes crediting dividends against Treasury senior preferred at its stated10% rate, with an additional approximately$25billion benefit to government beyond that return.

He assumes a2.5%capital standard and hypothetical Q4 2026 IPOs requiring approximately$30billion combined new capital. He estimates approximately$34 per-share intrinsic values and$31 IPO prices. His taxpayer proceeds estimate exceeds$300billion, assuming full warrant exercise and a sell-down over five years.

These inputs form a conditional bridge, not adopted policy:

| Necessary step | Status at cutoff |
|---|---|
| Treatment of senior preferred | Proposed credit/repayment interpretation, unresolved |
| Treasury warrants | Outstanding; dilution must be included |
| Capital standard and new issuance | Investor assumptions, not approved replacement rule |
| Relisting/IPO and release sequence | Not completed or finally agreed |
| Continuing federal support | Contractual/policy terms require resolution |

The January2 amendments add Treasury consent and public-input requirements. Existing holders therefore have stronger operating capital and a plausible political catalyst, but still face seniority, dilution and timing risk. A HOLD or ADD argument must explain why this changed probability distribution outweighs the rally and opportunity cost; it cannot rely solely on remembering the original cheap purchase.

drivers.driver: A second Trump administration creates a credible near-term path to release.
drivers.quote: What makes them particularly interesting today versus any other time in history is that there is a credible path for their removal from conservatorship in the relative short term, that is, in the next two years.

drivers.driver: Credit prior distributions toward repayment of senior preferred rather than leave an unlimited senior claim.
drivers.quote: the GSEs are credited with the dividends and other distributions paid on the government senior preferred

drivers.driver: Full Treasury warrant exercise aligns taxpayer proceeds with a successful offering.
drivers.quote: We calculate a profit to the gov’t of ~$300 billion assuming full exercise of its warrants and a sell down of common stock in both companies over the five years following the IPOs.

drivers.driver: Large conditional valuation upside remains despite rally, while outcome uncertainty requires limited exposure.
drivers.quote: We estimate the value of each company at the time of their IPOs in 2026 at ~$34 per share.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: January16 deck deliberately excluded. Original2013 purchase letter not authenticated; D00 uses attributed2015 retrospective letter. No direct new Trump commitment to exact terms verified. Freddie2021 netincome, complete peer multiples, current portfolio weights and52week prices omitted. Reason class uses harness-valid THESIS_ON_TRACK rather than S1-S5 because this is a hold.

final.company: the Company (Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac)
thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Essential guarantee franchise value: intact [D02, D04]
Earnings power and capital rebuild: strengthened [D03, D04]
Policy path toward recapitalization: improved (post-election catalyst) [D08, D09]
Shareholder participation: still contingent/unresolved [D02, D06, D10]
final.valuation_now: Market price of ~$6 represents a significant discount to the ~$34 intrinsic value scenario [D05, D10]

drivers.driver: The probability of a negotiated exit from conservatorship has materially improved with the new administration, aligning shareholder and taxpayer interests [D08, D09, D10].

final.memo:
Our investment in the GSEs remains a long-term, high-asymmetry proposition that has finally moved from a decade of stagnation toward a plausible policy resolution [D09, D10]. While the shares have rallied significantly since the November election, they continue to trade at a substantial discount to our estimated intrinsic value of approximately $34 per share under a successful recapitalization scenario [D05, D10]. The core franchises remain dominant, free-cash-flow-generative, and essential to the housing market, with balance sheets that have been significantly strengthened by years of retained earnings [D02, D03, D04].

Recent developments, including the change in the administration and the focus on a negotiated path to release from conservatorship, provide the catalyst we have long awaited [D08, D10]. Our thesis recognizes that the government holds the ultimate keys to the capital structure, and we acknowledge the inherent uncertainty, potential for dilution via Treasury warrants, and the new requirements for public input and Treasury consent [D02, D06, D08]. However, we view the current political environment as significantly more conducive to a solution that credits past Treasury payments and allows for a normalized private return [D09, D10].

We maintain our position with medium conviction because the path remains conditional on government negotiation rather than ordinary corporate execution [D09, D10]. We are not adding to the position at these levels, as we have already satisfied our required exposure while accounting for the significant remaining execution risk [D09]. We continue to heed the guidance that investors should limit exposure to what they can afford to lose, as political outcomes are rarely linear [D06, D09].
uncited_claims: The 25% forward IRR is an estimate based on the gap between current market prices and the identified $34 per-share scenario value over a multi-year horizon.

thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Policy path toward recapitalization: improved catalyst [D08], [D09]
final.valuation_now: Market price reflects early-stage optimism; intrinsic value estimated by management at ~$34/share based on hypothetical scenarios [D05], [D09]

drivers.driver: The election of a new administration provides a viable policy catalyst for recapitalization that was previously absent [D08], [D09].
Both enterprises have successfully rebuilt significant net worth while continuing to fulfill their essential guarantee function [D03], [D04].
While the recent rally reflects shifting expectations, the potential for an asymmetric return remains if the government adopts a negotiated recapitalization path [D05], [D06], [D09].

final.memo:
After more than a decade of ownership, the GSEs are finally approaching a potential inflection point [D09]. While our investment has not historically been a great success, the incoming administration offers a plausible path toward exiting conservatorship, a development that has long been the primary missing catalyst for realizing intrinsic value [D08], [D09]. The underlying guarantee businesses continue to prove their necessity and have successfully accumulated significant capital, strengthening the platform for a eventual recapitalization [D02], [D03].

We recognize the risks inherent in this position remain high, including uncertainty regarding the treatment of senior preferred liquidation preferences, warrant dilution, and the exact regulatory capital requirements that will be imposed [D02], [D06], [D10]. The recent amendments requiring Treasury consent for release, while adding procedural steps, do not break the thesis but rather underscore that any resolution must be a negotiated, orderly process [D06], [D08].

Given the significant appreciation since October, the market is beginning to price in a more favorable outcome, but we believe the gap between current prices and our estimated intrinsic value in a successful scenario remains sufficiently wide to justify maintaining our position [D05], [D09]. As we have cautioned, this remains a situation where shareholders should limit their exposure to what they can afford to lose, as political objectives may still diverge from shareholder outcomes [D06], [D09]. We maintain our conviction that the alignment of taxpayer and shareholder interests in a successful recapitalization remains the most logical path forward [D06].
